entries.title: We asked for your dream transit project. Here what you told us.
entries.summary: <p>We <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/transportation/2026/10/09/nita-cta-metra-pace-budget-dream-project" target="_blank" >asked readers</a> last week to share dream projects they want the Northern Illinois Transit Agency to prioritize for the CTA, Metra and Pace in next year's budget.</p><p>Many of you asked for a dedicated north-south corridor to connect L lines outside of Downtown. The idea echoes the Circle Line concept, something the <a class="Link" href="https://www.transitchicago.com/loop-the-loop---proposal-for-new-circle-line/" target="_blank" >CTA proposed</a> in 2002. Gavin Rosenzweig has his own name for it.</p><p>"My dream project is the Outer Loop Connect," Rosenzweig told the Chicago Sun-Times. The plan would connect "via dedicated [bus rapid transit] or subway, all of the CTA and Metra branch stations along Western Avenue. This would allow a much easier transfer between spokes of the rail service lines."</p><p>Here's some of what dozens of you told us.</p><h3>New east-west connections</h3><p>"They need to start considering creating a Light Blue Line, stretching from the Lawrence Red Line stop, over the top of Lawrence Avenue, all the way to the Jefferson Park L stop on the Blue Line."<br>— Scott Benson</p><p>"Extend the Pink Line to Navy Pier. Extend the Brown Line further west to Jefferson Park."<br>— Mario Lupo</p><p>"As a North Side resident, I would like to see a more direct route to O’Hare. The fact I am parallel with the airport, but I need to go all the way downtown via the Red to pick up the Blue (or the proposed express train) is just a nonstarter for early morning flights. Either the Brown Line needs to be extended to connect to the Blue, or [bus rapid transit] on Western connects with the Blue."<br>— Nick Murphy</p><h3>Bus improvements</h3><p>"The No. 74 Fullerton bus should be extended east to Cannon Drive."<br>— Daniel Joseph, Evanston</p><p>"I would like NITA to expand seating options at bus stops and train stations and improve the design of existing bus shelters."<br>— PC Smith</p><h3>Metra</h3><p>"I would like to see more frequent Metra trains, especially on the weekends. The two-hour lead times are brutal."<br>— Kari Winge</p><p>"Electrification of Metra rail, modernization of stations, cleanliness and actual security and fare enforcement."<br>— Dominik Wojtysiak</p><p>"Connect Red Line Extension directly to the Metra Electric Line. There must be a direct same-station transfer here."<br>— Roger Deschner</p><h3>Safety and accessibility </h3><p>"Spend the money on making all stations ADA accessible. This is a no-brainer. Especially the Blue Line."<br>— Peggy Skorich</p><p>"Improve Pace paratransit reliability and service [with] flexible scheduling."<br>— Jasmine O.</p><p>"Put more Cook County Sheriffs on the buses and L train turnstiles to make sure people pay a full fare. Especially on the routes that run 24/7. (Especially at night)."<br>— Michael Sessions</p><p>"I want them to remove the police from buses in Black and Brown communities. It does not make us safer. It just makes riding public transit uncomfortable. And make transit free for riders who pay too much for buses and train fares."<br>— Charity Parker</p><p>"Major cities all over the world have one car per train reserved for women and children so riders don’t experience sexual harassment (Mexico City, Tokyo, etc.). This would cost nothing. In fact, it would make money by increasing ridership significantly."<br>— Noel Stringham</p><h3>And one very creative suggestion</h3><p>"Gondolas [like an enclosed ski lift] are edging into the realm of public transport. So how about running a gondola line between O'Hare and Union Station?"<br>— Scott Summers</p>

entries.title: 74th Columbus Day Parade led by Tony Danza
entries.summary: <p>The Joint Civic Committee of Italian Americans' 74th Columbus Day Parade kicked off Downtown Monday morning, days after the group and Cook County Treasurer Maria Pappas welcomed a special delegation from Italy during a flag-raising celebration.</p><p>Grand marshaled by actors Tony Danza and Cristiana Dell'Anna, as well as Lou Gramm, the original singer of the band Foreigner, the parade kicked off at 11:30 a.m. at Wacker Drive and Dearborn Street — forced from its traditional spot on State Street due to construction.</p><p>Among those marching in the parade were the Campagna Youth Orchestra, a 34-piece group from Campania, Italy, the parade's annual region of honor this year.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item"
